name: Eagle Ford Midstream Expansion (NET Midstream)
researcher_notes: Separate from P0224. P0224 (NET Mexico, 124 mi, 42 in, FERC CP13-482) matches a different EIA project, 'Eagle Ford Shale Pipeline System Expansion', Historical Projects sheet row 782. This candidate is EIA Historical Projects row 746 of the August 2026 release: NET Midstream LLC, Expansion, Completed, in service May 2013, Texas intrastate, 105 mi, 24 in, no capacity given. So the other name on P0224 is not this line and may be worth a separate check. Natural Gas Intelligence (NGI) reports from 2012 describe a 105-mile, 24 and 30 inch extension of the existing Eagle Ford Midstream line for Anadarko from the Western Gas Brasada plant in LaSalle County to the Agua Dulce Hub, completion expected by April 2013. A NET Midstream 2015 SEC filing (NextEra Energy Partners) confirms NET Midstream owns 100 percent of the Eagle Ford pipeline, an intrastate line. NGI also gives the completed system as about 150 miles, mostly 30 inch. Diameter staged as 24 in per EIA; the NGI figure is 24 and 30 in. Parent system row not in the GEM roster, so PipelineName is a proposed parent name; the vetting team may prefer a different one. Owner name: NET Midstream not in gazetteer (nearest hit DT Midstream is a different company); legal form not found. NGI page text could not be re-read directly (403) though url_verifier passed it. Exact route not found; Texas Railroad Commission T-4 data not searched. Meets length rule (105 mi over 15.5 mi). Tier medium: two independent publishers (EIA and NGI) agree on length, but the 105 mi is the EIA/NGI planned figure and the NGI page was not directly readable.
